text:
Alex Newhook has become Montreal's Leafs killer, as Andrew Berkshire put it: two goals in Saturday's 4-2 win over Toronto, including a deflection off a Kaiden Guhle shot. Karine Hains of The Hockey News noted that his line doesn't play like a fourth line. Four of his five goals have come in his last ten games.

The scoring is real enough for a depth forward, but it's coming with a cost at the other end. The Canadiens have only 39% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 18 points worse than without him, the worst relative mark on the team. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season was the same: his line doesn't create much.

He's shooting 29% on 17 shots, which won't last. He's 25, a Cup winner with Colorado in 2022, and a useful penalty killer. Our projection sees about 20 goals, but we'd expect the next ten games to look quieter than the last ten.
